reason: The environment depicts signals directing cells along the fibroblast route, matching the goal.
expectation: The signals should guide some descendants toward a fibroblast population.

effect: The signals directed a subset toward fibroblasts and activated a collagen gene, producing messenger RNA for ribosomes.
reaction: The link between signaling and selective gene activity is clear; the mesoderm precursor is named but not explained.
reason: Amino acids are the building blocks ribosomes need to translate the collagen message.

choice.combine: Developing fibroblasts with collagen messenger RNA

expectation: The fibroblasts should use the RNA message and amino acids to make collagen protein precursors.

effect: The fibroblasts translated the collagen message into procollagen in the ER and Golgi; the next goal is to build extracellular material.
reaction: The RNA-to-protein connection is clear, though procollagen's role as a precursor is only implied.
reason: The secretory vesicles are shown carrying procollagen from the Golgi to the cell membrane.
expectation: The vesicles should release procollagen outside the fibroblasts for further processing.

effect: The vesicles released procollagen outside the fibroblasts, making it available for extracellular processing.
reaction: The connection between protein production and building the cells' surroundings is satisfying.
reason: The collagen-processing enzymes are shown clipping secreted procollagen and cross-linking the resulting collagen molecules.
expectation: The enzymes should process the procollagen into cross-linked collagen fibers.

effect: The enzymes produced cross-linked collagen fibers, whose pictured resistance to tension suggests a structural role.
reaction: The opposing arrows make the fibers' mechanical role clear.
reason: Hydrated proteoglycans are shown forming a water-rich gel around cells and collagen fibers, matching the extracellular-material goal.
expectation: The fibers and gel should form extracellular material around the cells.

effect: The collagen fibers and hydrated proteoglycans formed extracellular matrix around, rather than out of, the fibroblasts; the goal is complete.
reaction: The cell-versus-matrix inset makes that distinction clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the fibroblasts from gene activation through protein production and secretion was most worthwhile: it connects familiar gene expression to cells building their surroundings.

leastWorthwhile.text: The mesoderm precursor was named in the developmental sequence without an explanation, making that transition less accessible than the later protein-production steps.

surprise.text: The construction showed how secreted procollagen becomes tension-resistant fibers and then part of a gel-containing matrix outside the cells.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the pictured ingredients and goal made the sequence reasonably clear.

continue.text: I would continue to see how this extracellular material contributes to tissues and organs; the progression from cell activity to structure was interesting.
